Effects of Combined La–Ce Rare-Earth Treatment on the Hot-Rolled Microstructure and Texture of High-Grade Non-Oriented Electrical Steel
nodes.venue: Metals
nodes.abstract: This study compares high-grade non-oriented electrical steels without rare-earth addition and with a La-Ce combined rare-earth treatment. Optical microscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) were used to characterize the hot-rolled microstructure, through-thickness texture, and local orientation heterogeneity. The investigated La-Ce specimen exhibited a smaller average as-cast grain size (1.2 mm versus 2.0 mm) and a smaller hot-rolled surface grain size (39.08 μm versus 57.39 μm), together with a smoother microstructural transition from fine surface grains to elongated center-layer deformation grains. XRD revealed pronounced through-thickness texture gradients in both specimens. After a non-negativity-constrained post-reconstruction correction of the exported harmonic ODFs, the maximum α-fiber orientation density was 2.830 and 2.573 at the surface, 4.223 and 4.521 at 1/4 thickness, and 36.995 and 16.636 at the center for the rare-earth-free and La-Ce specimens, respectively. The center-layer difference corresponds to an approximately 55.0% lower α-fiber maximum in the investigated La-Ce specimen. For the γ-fiber, peak and mean f(g) values increased modestly at the surface and more strongly at 1/4 thickness, whereas the sampled ideal center-layer γ-fiber in the La-Ce specimen reached the lower bound of the constrained ODF representation. EBSD-IPF, GOS, and KAM maps further revealed reduced long-range orientation continuity and finer spatial segmentation of deformation-related orientation heterogeneity in the La-Ce specimen. Overall, the results show that trace La-Ce treatment is associated with microstructural refinement and a pronounced redistribution of the hot-band deformation texture, particularly in the sheet center.

nodes.name: Defect-Induced Negative Cooperative Adsorption on Plasmonic Heterointerfaces for Anti-Saturation Sensing of Bulky Emerging Contaminants
nodes.venue: Analytical Chemistry
nodes.abstract: Abstract Bulky emerging contaminants readily induce premature interface saturation, fundamentally limiting photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensors from simultaneously achieving ultrahigh sensitivity and a wide dynamic range. Herein, a defect-induced Au-sensitized WO3@FeWO4 heterointerface is proposed for the anti-saturation detection of the bulky contaminant rifampicin (RFP). The simultaneous regulation of oxygen and tungsten vacancies controls Au nucleation, promoting the exposure of highly active Au (311) facets to generate spatially heterogeneous active sites. The synergistic coupling between the heterojunction and the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect significantly accelerates charge separation, producing a strong initial PEC response. Crucially, this defect-facet coupled interface governs the adsorption dynamics of bulky RFP. The preferential occupation of high-activity sites triggers pronounced steric hindrance and repulsion, leading to negative cooperative adsorption (Hill coefficient = 0.318). This negative-feedback behavior effectively delays saturation, maintaining continuous interfacial responsiveness. Consequently, the sensor achieves an ultrawide linear range (1 nM to 150 μM) and an ultralow detection limit (0.76 nM). Ultimately, this work provides a novel method for monitoring bulky contaminants with high sensitivity and a broad linear range, successfully realizing real water sample analysis on a portable platform.

nodes.name: DSFormer: An Enhanced Dual-Selective Fusion Transformer Framework for Hyperspectral Image Classification++
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Hyperspectral image classification requires joint modeling of spectral signatures and spatial structure. In patch-based classification, each input patch is assigned the label of its center pixel, although neighboring pixels may belong to different land-cover classes. This setting motivates coordinating shallow spatial features, contextual refinement within the patch, and supervision of the resulting representation. We propose DSFormer++, an enhanced framework based on the original Dual Selective Fusion Transformer Network (DSFormer). Shallow Feature Compensation (SFC) combines shallow and patch-embedded features through gated residual fusion before the backbone. The Collaborative Global–Local (CGL) module applies an additional refinement operation with shared parameters before token selection at two backbone stages. Pixel Contrastive Loss (PCL) uses center-pixel labels to supervise projected patch embeddings during training. The proposed method achieves overall accuracies of 96.50%, 97.60%, 95.35%, and 94.83% on the Pavia University, Houston13, Indian Pines, and WHU-HH datasets, respectively. Component comparisons and approximately parameter-matched controls characterize configuration-dependent effects. Numerical checks assess consistency between the stated operations and their implementation, and an additional Botswana experiment extends the evaluation to a satellite wetland and woodland scene.

nodes.name: Cross-linguistic affective iconicity
nodes.abstract: Whether relationships between word form and affect reflect shared human constraints or language-specific conventions remains largely unresolved. Addressing this, here we tested whether affective mappings learned in one language zero-shot predict estimations for the emotional dimensions of valence and arousal in another using 85,375 lexical entries from ten languages diverse in origin and culture across eight (sub)lexical representations spanning orthographic, phonological, articulatory, and distributional semantic information. Results revealed a strong semantic transfer, greater for valence than arousal, while form-based transfer was smaller but consistently above zero across all seven representations for arousal, with the strongest effects for articulatory features. Language-distance analyses further revealed that valence-related orthographic and phoneme-bigram transfer was stronger between more closely related languages, particularly genealogically and the modest correspondence between fitted form coefficients indicated that transferable prediction coexisted with differences in feature weighting across languages. These findings characterize affective iconicity as graded and representation-dependent: valence generalizes most strongly through distributional meaning, whereas arousal leaves a more consistent cross-linguistic trace in word form. This pattern motivates an account in which culturally and historically shaped evaluative mappings coexist with activation-related mappings that may draw more broadly on shared embodied constraints, connecting linguistic form with the conceptual organization of affective experience.

nodes.name: Critical Success Factors in Developing Regional Multimodal Transportation Hubs Through Public-Private Partnerships
nodes.venue: Sustainability
nodes.abstract: Regional multimodal transportation hubs are strategic infrastructures for enhancing intermodal connectivity, regional competitiveness, and supply-chain resilience. Their development through Public–Private Partnerships (PPPs), however, requires coordination across institutional, infrastructural, financial, technological, and stakeholder domains. This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the critical success factors (CSFs) influencing the planning and development of a potential regional multimodal logistics hub through a PPP-type governance arrangement in Central Macedonia, Greece. An exploratory qualitative design was employed, based on questionnaire responses from 23 stakeholders and professionals across public authorities, business organizations, logistics and transport companies, construction and engineering firms, consultancies, and transport-infrastructure organizations. Responses were analyzed using theoretically informed reflexive thematic analysis. Six interrelated themes emerged: location and accessibility; infrastructure and technology; institutional and legal framework; financial sustainability and investment environment; stakeholder legitimacy and regional development; and adaptive sustainability. Findings highlight Central Macedonia’s strategic geographic advantages, particularly Thessaloniki’s gateway position, while distinguishing geographic potential from operational readiness. Successful development depends on reliable multimodal infrastructure, digital interoperability, institutional coordination, regulatory stability, credible demand and financing, effective public–private cooperation, stakeholder legitimacy, and adaptive capacity. In the Central Macedonia case, perceived implementation readiness emerges from the interaction of these conditions rather than from any single factor in isolation.

nodes.name: Compressed Time, Narrow Space: The Visual-Temporal Aesthetics of Mobile Microdrama on ReelShort
nodes.venue: Mobile Media & Communication
nodes.abstract: The widespread adoption of digital platforms and mobile devices has significantly transformed audiovisual storytelling. Short-form mobile microdramas represent not only a new mode of distribution but also a narrative form that reorganizes cinematic time and space. While previous research has primarily focused on platform economies, audience engagement, and algorithmic circulation, the visual-temporal organization of mobile microdramas has received comparatively little attention from the perspective of quantitative film analysis. Addressing this gap, this study investigates how mobile microdramas reorganize cinematic form through temporal compression and spatial narrowing. A quantitative formal analysis was conducted on the first episodes of 10 ReelShort series representing different narrative tropes. The analysis examined average shot length (ASL), editing rhythm, shots per minute, shot-scale distribution, and the use of establishing shots. Shot boundaries were automatically identified using Adobe Premiere Pro's Scene Edit Detection tool, while shot scales and spatial indicators were analysed through qualitative coding. The findings show that an exceptionally short ASL of 2.31 s, together with the predominance of medium shots and the limited use of full/long shots and establishing shots, minimizes spatial exposition while privileging character-centred compositions and producing a dense visual rhythm optimized for smartphone viewing. The results suggest that ReelShort reorganizes cinematic form by simultaneously compressing cinematic time and narrowing cinematic space, extending long-term stylistic tendencies in film history while adapting them to the perceptual and technological conditions of vertically oriented mobile media.

nodes.name: Beyond site-specific archaeological prospection: Spectral-geometry reveals cross-site cropmark signals in satellite data
nodes.venue: PNAS Nexus
nodes.abstract: Abstract Remote sensing has long supported archaeological prospection, mainly through the detection of cropmarks, a key archaeological proxy expressed as spectral vegetation anomalies over subsurface features. Yet, cropmark detection is still assumed in the literature to be highly site-specific, governed by local agronomic and environmental conditions. Using multispectral Sentinel-2 data from three European archaeological sites, we show that models trained in one landscape can recover meaningful archaeological proxy signals in other locations. By relying strictly on satellite spectral signatures for training, our models achieve measurable cross-location transferability without incorporating ancillary environmental data. We find that cross-site performance arises not from geographic proximity but from the spectral-geometric similarity of vegetation responses, and that transferability is strongly directional. We quantify this relationship through a Directional Strength Score (DSS), derived from monthly subcluster distances under multiple norms, which captures directional geometric similarity and correlates strongly with machine-learning performance. To keep the analysis grounded in the underlying spectral signal, we relied on architecturally restrained nonlinear classifiers (SVM and constrained XGBoost) and used NDVI-identified phenophases to align training and evaluation with comparable seasonal windows. Taken together, these results demonstrate that partial, spectrally mediated cross-location cropmark detection is feasible and that the underlying vegetation responses exhibit stable spectral structure, with spectral geometry offering a clear interpretive lens on why these signals can transfer across sites. Leveraging globally harmonized satellite data, this approach offers a scalable complement to uneven historical aerial archives and supports systematic regional archaeological prioritization to be deployed within integrated archaeological workflows.

nodes.name: Artificial Intelligence, Foundation Models, and Digital Twins for Climate-Resilient Agriculture: A Review
nodes.venue: Intelligent Agriculture
nodes.abstract: Climate change, increasing food demand, and resource constraints are accelerating the transition from conventional precision agriculture toward smart, autonomous, and climate-resilient agricultural systems. Artificial intelligence (AI), foundation models, digital twins (DTs), the Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, edge–cloud computing, and big data analytics are emerging as key technologies for data-driven agricultural management. This review critically evaluates recent advances in AI-driven intelligent agriculture, with emphasis on machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI (XAI), generative and agentic AI, multimodal foundation models, and digital twins, together with the sensing and computing infrastructures required for their deployment. Relevant literature was identified using keywords related to AI, foundation models, digital twins, IoT, precision agriculture, and climate-resilient agriculture, with emphasis on recent peer-reviewed studies addressing technological applications, performance, limitations, challenges, and future prospects. The selected literature was critically synthesized to identify technological trends, knowledge gaps, and emerging research opportunities. The review highlights that the greatest potential of intelligent agriculture lies in integrating heterogeneous data from sensors, UAVs (unmanned aerial vehicles), satellites, weather systems, field operations, and agricultural knowledge to support context-aware prediction, decision-making, and autonomous action. However, data quality, model generalizability, explainability, interoperability, cybersecurity, computational requirements, and large-scale field validation remain major challenges. This review further develops an integrated perspective connecting AI, foundation models, multimodal data infrastructures, digital twins, and autonomous agricultural systems within a unified cyber-physical ecosystem. Future priorities include trustworthy AI, agentic decision-making, semantic interoperability, federated learning, continuous learning, and self-learning digital twins toward Agriculture 6.0.

nodes.name: An Optimized Audio–Visual Deepfake Detection Framework Using Mamba Vision Transformers with Linear Complexity
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: The rise of advanced deepfake technologies presents new challenges to media authenticity, making it harder to spot manipulated videos through traditional approaches. Current approaches have a quadratic time complexity O(n2), poor cross-dataset generalization with 20 to 35% accuracy degradation, and inadequate audio–visual fusion mechanisms. This paper presents Mamba-AVGuard, a novel audio–visual deepfake detection framework leveraging Mamba Vision Transformers with selective state-space modeling to achieve linear O(n) complexity within the Mamba encoder streams. The novel framework combines a 12-layer visual Mamba encoder for spatial and temporal facial inconsistency analysis with an 8-layer lightweight audio Mamba encoder for prosodic inconsistency analysis, fused via a cross-modal attention block with ±33 ms temporal synchronization. Experiments conducted on two large-scale audio–visual deepfake benchmarks, FakeAVCeleb and AV-Deepfake1M, demonstrate that Mamba-AVGuard outperforms compared methods with 99.92% in-dataset accuracy and 98.47% cross-dataset accuracy on these two benchmarks. The system achieves a processing speed of less than 1.8 s for 30-s videos, with 56% less memory than the best competing transformer-based method, facilitating a throughput of more than 1200 videos per hour for social media verification and forensic workstations.

nodes.name: AMSSE-SwinTrans: A harmonized multimodal hybrid framework with explainable AI for ischemic stroke lesion segmentation
nodes.venue: Technology and Health Care
nodes.abstract: Background Accurate ischemic stroke lesion segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is important but challenging due to variability in lesion morphology. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) effectively capture local spatial features but often struggle to capture long-range contextual dependencies needed for irregular lesions. Transformer-based architectures are good at capturing global context; however, they are computationally expensive and difficult to deploy in resource-constrained environments. The black-box nature of deep learning models limits their clinical adoption owing to lack of transparency. Objective This study introduces AMSSE-SwinTrans, a lightweight hybrid CNN-Transformer framework to make stroke lesion segmentation accurate, efficient and interpretable across different MRI modalities. Methods This study proposes AMSSE-SwinTrans, a lightweight hybrid CNN-Transformer framework that combines adaptive multi-scale squeeze-and-excitation (AMSSE) module with simplified transformer blocks employing multi-head self-attention, along with explainable AI (XAI) for clinical interpretation. The model was evaluated on a single-channel harmonized multimodal two-dimensional MRI Slices from ATLAS v2.0 and ISLES 2022 dataset. Results The model achieved an overall Dice of 0.8629, lesion-specific Dice of 0.7535. An ablation study demonstrated a significant performance improvement when each component was added. The model comparisons were all significant with Wilcoxon signed-rank test yielding p-value ( p < 0.001) across all comparisons. With only 27.67 M parameters, 17.67 GFLOPs, and 9.22 ms inference time per slice, the architecture is well-suited for deployment in resource-constrained clinical settings. The interpretability of the model is supported by Attention Rollout and Grad-CAM++ visualizations. Conclusion AMSSE-SwinTrans establishes itself as a resource-efficient and interpretable framework for multimodal stroke lesion segmentation.

nodes.name: AI-Based Driver Drowsiness Detection Using Image Enhancement and Swin Transformer
nodes.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
nodes.abstract: This study introduces a smart system designed to detect driver drowsiness in real time, focusing mainly on checking whether a driver's eyes are closed for an unusually long period. While conventional AI image detection methods (like standard CNNs) often fail when faced with poor lighting, motion blur, noisy images, or deliberate visual distortions (adversarial attacks), this solution solves these issues by combining two advanced techniques: Diffusion-Based Denoising (U-Net Architecture): Acts as a preprocessing cleanup layer. Before analyzing the image, it strips away visual noise, blur, and distortion, turning corrupted camera frames into clear, high-quality images. Swin Transformer Model: Serves as the primary classification engine. It uses a multi-scale, window-based attention mechanism to accurately detect eye states (open vs. closed) across both fullface images and close-up eye patches. To make the AI more resilient to unpredictable driving conditions, the researchers trained it using artificial image modifications (like rotation, zooming, and shifting) along with simulated visual attacks.

nodes.name: Shravani Suresh Kutal, P. A. Sawant, Dr. H. B. Jadhav
International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
A Review of Machine Learning in Species Distribution Modeling under Climate Change in West Africa
nodes.venue: Asian Journal of Geographical Research
nodes.abstract: Species distribution modelling (SDM) has become a central instrument for anticipating how biodiversity is redistributed under climate change, and machine learning now supplies most of the algorithmic capacity behind these predictions. West Africa combines high climatic exposure, dense reliance on wild biological resources, and thin biodiversity records, so the region is a demanding setting in which the strengths and weaknesses of machine learning SDMs are exposed. Scope. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026 were synthesised to describe how correlative SDMs, tree-based ensembles, and deep learning have been applied to West African flora, fauna, disease vectors, and agricultural pests, and to assess the treatment of data quality, model transferability, and reporting standards. Key findings. Maximum entropy modelling remains the dominant approach, yet tree-based ensembles and, more recently, deep neural networks are being adopted where occurrence volume permits. Reported discrimination is high across algorithm families, with area under the curve values frequently above 0.90, though internal validation was shown to overstate reliability when sampling bias and extrapolation into novel climates were left uncorrected. Plant studies concentrated in Benin, Togo, Nigeria, and Burkina Faso projected habitat contraction for a majority of exploited woody species, with northward and upslope displacement of suitable conditions, while vector and pest models projected expansion of climatically suitable areas for several malaria vectors and invasive insects across the region. Persistent occurrence-data scarcity, spatial sampling bias, and inconsistent reporting were identified as the leading constraints on inference. Implications. Bias-aware calibration, spatially independent validation, standardised reporting, and investment in regional occurrence data are needed before machine learning SDMs are used to guide conservation prioritisation, protected-area design, and public-health planning in West Africa. This review positions the regional evidence within methodological developments and defines data-supported priorities for the next phase of work.

nodes.name: A Point Cloud Transformer-Based Regression Approach for Estimating Above-Ground Biomass from 3D Point Clouds
nodes.venue: Engineering Perspective
nodes.abstract: From the perspective of global food security, the estimation of crop biomass and yield is a critical process. Traditionally, plant height is manually measured using field samples for biomass and yield estimation, and plant samples are cut, dried, and weighed. This labor-intensive process can be made more efficient through advanced technologies integrated into modern agricultural machinery. One such technology, light detection and ranging (LiDAR), provides nondestructive 3D point clouds with millimeter-level accuracy. However, processing this data is highly challenging due to the complex canopy architecture of cereal crops. Therefore, deep learning architectures can be used to effectively analyze 3D point cloud data. In this context, a deep learning-based regression approach was proposed to estimate above-ground biomass from 3D point cloud data. This study employed a point cloud transformer (PCT) architecture. Growth Stage-PCT (GS-PCT) models were developed by integrating growth stage information into the proposed Small, Base, and Deep variants of the PCT architecture. According to the experimental results, when both growth stages were evaluated together, the proposed GS-PCT-Small model achieved the best performance, with an R² of 0.95, an RMSE of 88.60 g m⁻², an MAE of 69.34 g m⁻², and a MAPE of 13.69%. During the vegetative stage, the PCT-Small model achieved an RMSE of 58.52 g m⁻², while during the flowering stage, the GS-PCT-Small model achieved an RMSE of 111.55 g m⁻². The findings indicate that the models achieved high predictive performance for above-ground biomass estimation from 3D point clouds.

nodes.name: A Hierarchical Framework for Arctic Shoreline Type Mapping Using SAR and Optical Satellite Imagery
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Although intertidal-zone delineation and shoreline or coastal geomorphological classification have been extensively investigated, relatively few studies have integrated these complementary information layers within a unified and operational remote-sensing framework for oil-spill emergency response. With increasing development and marine transportation activities in the Arctic, detailed and spatially explicit shoreline information is essential for oil-spill response planning and coastal hazard assessment along the Canadian Arctic coast. A key challenge is to reliably characterize the spatial extent and geomorphological variability of Arctic intertidal shorelines under substantial temporal variability in tidal inundation and environmental conditions. This study presents a hierarchical shoreline classification framework designed to support oil-spill emergency preparedness and response planning. The framework integrates Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) backscatter, temporal-change and structural descriptors, and Sentinel-2 water-sensitive indices to derive a composite shore-zone proxy that captures spatial and temporal information on tidal inundation and coastal surface characteristics. This proxy supports Level 1 shore-zone mapping, while high-resolution optical imagery enables subsequent Level 2 shoreline-type classification. The framework was evaluated in four Canadian Arctic coastal areas representing diverse coastal landscapes and environmental conditions, including differences in tidal regimes, water turbidity, floating ice, and geomorphology. Results indicated that mapping accuracy remains constrained for tidal zones and substrates smaller than or comparable to the sensor’s spatial resolution. For Level 1 shore-zone mapping, unsupervised classification of the temporal and composite indices achieved overall mapping accuracies of 56–73% for the Upper Shore Zone across three study areas. For Level 2 shoreline-type mapping, Random Forest classification of high-resolution satellite imagery, including WorldView and GeoEye imagery, achieved overall accuracies of 81–85% across the four study areas. These results demonstrate the potential of the composite shore-zone proxy to integrate complementary SAR and optical information for consistent characterization of Arctic shore zones, while the subsequent shoreline-type classification provides additional geomorphological detail. Together, the hierarchical products provide spatially explicit shoreline information that can support the identification and prioritization of shoreline areas for oil-spill response planning and resource allocation.

nodes.name: Spatial transcriptomics elucidates trajectories associated with transformation in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors
nodes.venue: Neuro-Oncology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Tumor invasion and malignant transformation are spatiotemporally coordinated processes that shape clinical behavior, diagnostic classification, and treatment response. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) are aggressive tumors that can arise sporadically or in people with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF-1) yet how distinct spatial niches underlie MPNST intra-tumor heterogeneity, local invasion or malignant transformation from benign precursors are not fully understood. Methods We integrate spatial analysis of 50,896 transcriptomes from 15 human MPNSTs with deep learning image analysis to define the interplay between genetic alterations, the immune microenvironment, and epigenetic cell fate regulation in MPNST invasion and transformation. Results Spatial transcriptomics reveal distinct infiltrating immune cells and immunomodulatory spatial clusters in sporadic compared to NF-1 associated MPNSTs. Local invasion is marked by spatially defined immunomodulatory and dedifferentiation programs. Analysis of two NF-1 associated MPNSTs with contiguous morphologically defined neurofibroma and MPNST components demonstrates NF-1 associated tumors identified a similar malignant transformation process associated with dynamic immune infiltration, chromosome 9p loss, and dedifferentiation concomitant with increased cell proliferation. Finally, deep learning morphology encoders were trained on spatial transcriptomic data to predict spatial transcriptomic cluster identity and chromosome 9p loss from hematoxylin and eosin stained (H&E) images although the generalizability of such encoders remains a challenge. Conclusions Our data provide a spatial framework for peripheral nerve sheath tumor transformation although the limited sample size of the present cohort will require additional validation of the proposed model.

nodes.name: Phenology-driven multisensor unsupervised crop mapping in data-scarce irrigated agriculture: a case of Adea District in Ethiopia
nodes.venue: Water Practice & Technology
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate irrigation planning, water allocation, and agricultural productivity assessment are frequently constrained in data-scare regions where reliable ground-based crop information and spatial coverage data are limited. This study addresses these gaps using a phenology-driven, multisensor unsupervised crop-mapping framework implemented within Google Earth Engine (GEE). The approach integrates monthly normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) profiles from Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1VV backscatter, and digital elevation model–derived terrain slope into unsupervised K-means clustering algorithm. Adea District, Ethiopia, served as a demonstration site to evaluate and interpret the phenological signatures of key irrigated crops. The identified crop types were mapped to estimate spatial coverage and compared with the ground truth observations of irrigated wheat and tomato fields. The approach successfully distinguished irrigated wheat and tomato fields with an overall classification accuracy of 91%, a Kappa coefficient of 0.82, and estimated cultivated areas of 666.93 and 812.35 ha, respectively. Combining phenological profiles with multisensor satellite observations significantly enhance unsupervised classification performance in heterogeneous, smallholder-dominated agricultural landscapes. The cloud-based framework offers a computationally scalable and cost-effective solution for crop mapping, and water productivity monitoring in data-scarce agricultural regions.

nodes.name: Backlighting the Universe with Fast Radio Bursts: An Anthology of Dispersion Measure Cross Correlations with Tracers of Large-scale Structure and Baryonic Matter
nodes.venue: The Astrophysical Journal
nodes.abstract: Abstract Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe baryons permeating the cosmic web through their dispersion measures (DMs), which encode the integrated electron density along cosmological sight lines. Using 3455 unique FRB sources from CHIME/FRB with ∼15′ localizations, we present an anthology of DM correlations with tracers of large-scale structure and baryonic matter at redshifts z ≲ 1.5. We measured correlations with a vector signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 2.4–5 with 10 probes, including galaxies (2.8), weak gravitational lensing (2.6), cosmic infrared background (4.0), cosmic microwave background (CMB) lensing (3.3), the thermal Sunyaev–Zel’dovich (tSZ) effect (3.8), X-ray emission tracing galaxy clusters (5.0) and superclusters (3.3), soft X-ray background (SXRB, 4.1), and radio continuum emission (3.0). These measurements reveal a consistent picture in which FRB sight lines intersecting overdense environments carry systematically larger DMs. Correlations with hot-gas tracers provide additional leverage on the strength of feedback, as they are strongly weighted toward the dense, bound gas. The measured amplitude of tSZ×DM and SXRB×DM correlations is consistent with theoretical predictions of baryon distribution from a DM– z relation-inferred model with moderate feedback at a ∼0.5 σ level. A weaker feedback scenario is disfavored at ∼3.5 σ by the SXRB×DM correlation under our adopted modeling assumptions. Taken together, these measurements constitute a quantitative multitracer foundation for a new era in which FRBs from next-generation facilities, such as BURSTT, CHORD, the Deep Synoptic Array, and the Square Kilometer Array, in harmony with other probes, will map the baryon content of the full extent of the cosmic web.

nodes.name: Uncertainty Characterization Framework for Machine Learning Based ACM in Q‐Band Satellite Links
nodes.venue: International Journal of Satellite Communications and Networking
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Adaptive coding and modulation (ACM) is a widely utilized technique in satellite communication networks to mitigate the adverse effects of rain fades, particularly in extremely high frequency (EHF) bands. As a core component of fade mitigation techniques (FMTs), ACM improves signal resilience. However, its effectiveness is constrained by reliance on non‐real‐time channel state information. To overcome this limitation, this study explores the use of deep learning (DL) algorithms to predict rain attenuation, enabling more efficient and optimal selection of modulation and coding (MODCOD) schemes within the ACM framework. We present a comparative analysis of nine DL models for rain attenuation prediction, using Q‐band measurements from the Alphasat satellite, recorded at Chilbolton Observatory, UK. Furthermore, we incorporate Monte Carlo (MC) dropout‐based uncertainty quantification (UQ) into MODCOD selection, demonstrating its advantage over conventional approaches lacking UQ. Results show that integrating UQ enhances throughput, particularly in models such as gated recurrent units (GRUs). This work proposes a practical framework for UQ‐driven adaptive MODCOD selection in DVB‐RCS2 systems.

nodes.name: International Journal of Satellite Communications and Networking
Toward physics‑consistent NIIRS prediction using the targeting task performance metric
nodes.abstract: The National Image Interpretability Rating Scale (NIIRS) remains the dominant performance language for optical remote-sensing systems, yet its primary prediction tool, the General Image Quality Equation (GIQE), is increasingly misaligned with modern digital imagers. GIQE's empirical structure combines hardcopy-era NIIRS psychophysics with a regression calibrated on electro-optical imagery delivered as standardized, contrast-optimized hardcopy, where system performance was reduced to a small set of adjustable parameters and a limited representation of modulation transfer. In contrast, contemporary spaceborne imaging systems exhibit complex interactions among optics, detectors, sampling, processing, and noise that are not naturally captured by GIQE's formulation. In this paper, we propose and specify a development path for NIIRS prediction based on the Targeting Task Performance (TTP) metric. This approach directly benefits the rapidly growing class of small-satellite imaging systems by providing a scalable, physics-consistent framework for sensor design trades, on-orbit performance prediction, and mission-level interpretability assessment. TTP is itself grounded in extensive psychophysical analysis, is tightly coupled to imaging-system physics, and has seen two decades of U.S. Army use and published validation for predicting target-acquisition performance. Unlike GIQE, TTP incorporates the full spatial-frequency response of the imaging chain, optionally including the human visual response and display resolution, rather than reducing system performance to only three scalar measures: GSD, RER, and noise. We propose a method for mapping NIIRS criteria to representative target size or area, contrast, and task-difficulty calibration, evaluating criterion-level task probabilities, and calibrating their aggregation into an ordinal or fractional NIIRS estimate. This provides a physics-consistent path for evaluating modern remote-sensing architectures that can be separately tuned for prediction under human analysis or AI/ML.

nodes.name: SubTerrAInNet: A Multimodal CNN-GNN Framework for Collapse Susceptibility Prediction in Underground Mining Tunnels
nodes.venue: International Journal of Advanced Trends in Computer Science and Engineering
nodes.abstract: The collapse of underground mine workings remains a severe safety problem in artisanal and small-scale mining, where engineered ground support, geotechnical instrumentation, and systematic rock-mass characterization are often unavailable. Motivated by the 12 August 2026 Kassa mine-pit collapse in Barkin Ladi, Plateau State, this study presents SubTerrAInNet, a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates high-resolution tunnel imagery with low-cost geological and structural observations for segment-level collapse-susceptibility classification. The visual stream uses a transfer-learned Residual Network-50 (ResNet-50) convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract image signatures associated with cracking, seepage staining, weathering, and spalling, while a graph neural network (GNN) encodes tunnel geometry, overburden, joint orientation, water condition, crack density, and inter-segment connectivity. The dataset comprises 8,500 RGB images linked to 264 annotated tunnel segments from 15 abandoned workings in the Jos Plateau. Partitioning was performed group-wise at the physical-site level: each mine site was assigned exclusively to training, validation, or hold-out testing, so that no tunnel segment or image from a given site occurred in more than one partition. On the reported hold-out test set, SubTerrAInNet achieved 91.82% accuracy, an F1-score of 0.88, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.95. This represents a 2.82-percentage-point accuracy gain over the best conventional baseline, Extremely Randomized Trees (89.0%), and a 1.62-point gain over the strongest reported deep learning baseline, long short-term memory with attention (LSTM-Attention; 90.2%). Ablation results further show that multimodal fusion outperforms CNN-only and GNN-only variants. The final evaluation also considers collapse-class sensitivity, specificity, precision, precision- recall area under the curve (PR-AUC), probability calibration, and bootstrap confidence intervals. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) is used to relate image-driven predictions to visible degradation precursors. SubTerrAInNet therefore provides a resource-aware framework for camera-assisted hazard screening, although prospective external validation, calibrated uncertainty estimation, and engineering review remain necessary before operational deployment.

nodes.name: International Journal of Advanced Trends in Computer Science and Engineering
Smart Agriculture and Environmental Monitoring: An Edge-AI, IoT, and Federated Learning Framework for Climate-Resilient Farming
nodes.venue: American Journal of Environmental Science and Engineering
nodes.abstract: This study presents a system architecture, algorithm, and evaluation protocol for smart agriculture and environmental monitoring. It is a method/architecture contribution and does not report field trial results. World food production is still under stress from climate variability, the availability of freshwater resources, and the cost of farm inputs, offering an incentive to transition to data-driven and sensor-based farm management practices. Internet of Things (IoT)-based agricultural monitoring is well developed, but most systems deployed focus on a single parameter (e.g., soil moisture) or the parameter is inferred solely in the cloud, adding latency and fragility to the deployment of systems in rural areas. In this study, we propose an integrated architecture for low-power multiparameter environmental sensing, LoRaWAN/NB-IoT connectivity, edge-based lightweight inference, and privacy-preserving federated learning with cross-farm model aggregation, which is further complemented by a digital twin layer for scenario simulation. The decision layer of the framework can combine data from ground sensors with UAV and satellite images for the multi-scale monitoring of crop health and environmental quality (air, water, and GHG proxies). We contribute the full system design, an algorithmic pipeline, a sensor and model configuration specification, and a pre-registered evaluation protocol intended to guide future field deployment; no field data have yet been collected and clearly labelled non-empirical templates showing the expected reporting format only, rather than measured outcomes. The architecture and protocol are instead grounded in, and cross-checked against, published state-of-the-art results, which report an accuracy range of 82–97% for federated crop-yield prediction and 20–30% water savings from sensor-controlled irrigation.

Scalable Information Dynamics (SID): A Novel Paradigm for Predicting Non-Stationary Complex Systems
nodes.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
nodes.abstract: Scalable Information Dynamics (SID): A Novel Paradigm for Predicting Non-Stationary Complex Systems Abstract This document introduces Scalable Information Dynamics (SID), a foundational theoretical framework that redefines information capacity as a dynamic, state-dependent variable rather than a fixed constant. Unlike classical information theory, which treats capacity as determined by hardware or noise limits, SID posits that a system’s ability to encode, process, and transmit meaningful information scales with its instantaneous rate of change and contextual complexity. This paradigm resolves the long-standing paradox that chaotic systems are sources of noise rather than high-density information carriers. By quantifying information transfer and memory adaptation in real-time, SID enables accurate prediction of extreme events in non-stationary domains — from atmospheric turbulence to financial crashes — while offering a unified mathematical language for adaptive intelligence across biological and artificial systems. The core innovation lies in the formulation of two key functions: the Information Transfer Function (ITF) and the Dynamic Memory Function (DMF), which together allow systems to scale computational resources dynamically, optimizing efficiency without sacrificing predictive power during volatility. 1. Introduction: The Dynamic Nature of Information Classical information theory, rooted in Shannon’s work, defines channel capacity as a fixed parameter constrained by bandwidth or noise floor. Yet in complex, evolving systems — such as weather patterns, financial markets, or neural networks — this static view fails. SID proposes a radical departure: information capacity C(t) is not an invariant but a dynamic variable intrinsic to the system’s state at time t. This transforms information from a static resource into a fluid, context-sensitive property that expands or contracts with volatility. The central tenet of SID is: “The greater the dynamic complexity and volatility of a system’s state, the higher its intrinsic capacity to encode, process, and transmit predictive information.” This inverts the conventional intuition that chaos equals noise — instead, SID identifies chaos as a state of maximal informational potential, where rapid evolution encodes dense, high-resolution signals about future trajectories. This is not merely a refinement. It is a redefinition — one that repositions information not as an output of a channel, but as a property of the system’s temporal evolution. This is the first framework to treat information capacity as a state function, not a parameter — a conceptual leap that unifies physics, biology, and artificial intelligence under a single, scalable logic. 2. Theoretical Foundations and Core Formulations The mathematical architecture of SID is built upon three core variables describing a system’s instantaneous information dynamics: Rate of Change Magnitude (|ΔTobs/Δt|): This quantifies the speed at which observable system states evolve. In SID, this is the primary driver of information generation — rapid change implies high information density, not noise. Contextual Scaling Factor (βcontextual): This factor adjusts the system’s internal sensitivity to environmental complexity — acting as an adaptive amplifier or dampener — without requiring fixed thresholds. It is not a pre-defined constant, but a system-dependent variable computed from real-time context. Dynamic Complexity Metric (DCM): This measures the intrinsic non-linearity and internal structure of the system — serving as a baseline for potential information richness — and is used to normalize the ITF. SID defines the Information Transfer Function (ITF) as: ITF(t) ∝ |ΔTobs/Δt| ⋅ ln(βcontextual / βbase) Here, βbase is a system-specific reference level of complexity (e.g., historical baseline, equilibrium state, or statistical average). The logarithmic scaling ensures that relative increases in contextual complexity produce non-linear, exponential gains in information processing capacity — capturing subtle patterns invisible to linear models. SID also introduces the Dynamic Memory Function (DMF), which governs the adaptive retention of past information: During high volatility → memory window shrinks → focus on immediate changes During stability → memory window expands → consolidation of long-term trends Unlike traditional models with fixed memory windows, DMF is state-dependent, allowing systems to optimize computational effort and predictive accuracy dynamically. This enables resource-efficient operation — reducing energy consumption by up to 90% during stable phases — while maintaining peak performance during critical transitions. 3. Bridging Physics, Information Theory, and Complex Systems SID unifies three domains under one formalism — not by merging ideas, but by redefining their common language. It resolves the “paradox of information in chaotic systems” by showing that chaos is not a barrier to prediction, but a source of high-resolution signals. This allows SID to model phenomena across disciplines without ad hoc assumptions: Atmospheric Dynamics: Hurricanes or tornadoes emerge from accelerating gradients of pressure and temperature — SID detects these accelerations as information-rich precursors, enabling lead-time prediction. This is exemplified empirically by the Atmospheric Transition Entropy (ATE) v9.0 — a validated, reproducible application of SID’s core principles in meteorology. ATE v9.0 demonstrates how SID’s dynamic scaling and contextual adjustment translate into operational forecasting with sub-1.5% relative error across five global case studies — including extreme events like Hurricane Ophelia at Mace Head. Its architecture, which treats atmospheric evolution as a continuous transition rather than static observations, mirrors SID’s foundational claim that information resides in change, not in equilibrium. Financial Markets: Systemic risk is signaled not by volatility alone, but by the rate of change in volatility — SID identifies early warning signals before crashes. The ITF quantifies this acceleration in market dynamics, while DMF adapts memory windows to capture short-term momentum versus long-term trends — a mechanism directly applicable to algorithmic trading and portfolio risk management. Biological Systems: Organisms adapt via dynamic information processing — SID models the nervous system as a context-sensitive interface to volatile environments. Neural plasticity, sensory adaptation, and behavioral switching are all manifestations of state-dependent information capacity — aligning perfectly with SID’s framework where βcontextual acts as an internal modulator of response strength. Artificial Intelligence: Neural networks can adapt their architecture and memory depth in real-time — SID provides the theoretical basis for “self-scaling” AI architectures. The ITF would guide resource allocation in deep learning systems under uncertainty; DMF would control temporal granularity in attention mechanisms or recurrent layers — making SID a foundational tool for next-generation adaptive intelligence. This is not incremental progress — it is structural redefinition. The framework does not merely apply existing tools; it replaces the assumption of static information with one of dynamic, context-sensitive capacity — a shift that reconfigures how we model physical, biological, and artificial systems. 4. Practical Applications and Computational Efficiency SID enables real-time, resource-aware prediction and decision-making in volatile environments: Extreme Event Forecasting: In meteorology, SID predicts hurricanes by detecting acceleration of pressure gradients — providing days of lead time for disaster preparedness. This capability is operationalized in ATE v9.0, which has demonstrated high precision across diverse atmospheric regimes. Financial Risk Management: Early detection of volatility acceleration allows proactive portfolio adjustments. By applying SID’s ITF, financial models can quantify how fast asset correlations or price variances are changing — not just their magnitude — enabling traders to anticipate regime shifts before they materialize. The DMF component then adjusts the memory horizon: during periods of market calm, longer-term trends are preserved; during turbulence, only immediate signals are processed — reducing computational load while preserving predictive accuracy. Autonomous Robotics: Robots dynamically scale computational resources based on environmental complexity — improving response time and energy efficiency. For example, a drone navigating through dense urban traffic uses minimal memory during stable flight but triggers full sensor fusion when encountering sudden obstacles — mirroring SID’s adaptive memory strategy. Neural Network Optimization: Adaptive architectures scale in real-time — operating conservatively during stable phases, expanding during high-density data events. SID provides the underlying logic for neural architecture search (NAS) systems that adjust depth, width, and attention mechanisms based on information density — turning “adaptive intelligence” from a metaphor into a scalable algorithmic principle. Computational efficiency is a direct result of SID’s dynamic scaling. By shortening memory windows during volatility, systems avoid processing redundant information. During stability, they conserve energy by reducing complexity. This adaptability makes SID ideal for embedded systems — satellites, drones, IoT — where energy and bandwidth are constrained. 5. Preclinical evaluation of a safety-aware multimodal robotic pipeline for human–robot interaction in post-stroke rehabilitation
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Digital Health
nodes.abstract: Introduction Post-stroke rehabilitation increasingly requires technologies capable of supporting intensive, measurable, and adaptable interventions while preserving clinical supervision and patient safety. This study presents a lightweight, safety-aware, and modular multimodal robotic pipeline for embodied human–robot interaction in post-stroke rehabilitation, with a first target application in hemispatial inattention. Methods The system was implemented on the TIAGo mobile manipulator within a ROS 2-based architecture and integrates therapist-mediated supervision, speech-based and graphical interaction, head-orientation monitoring, adaptive auditory recall, robot-mediated and screen-based task delivery, and structured performance logging. Dialogue management is based on a deterministic finite-state machine coupled with a rule-based Natural Language Understanding pipeline, enabling predictable interaction handling, explicit fallback behavior, and therapist escalation for safety-relevant events. A preliminary preclinical evaluation was conducted in 16 healthy participants, with a repeated acquisition after 1 month. The study assessed operational feasibility, multimodal interaction robustness, head-orientation monitoring stability, task execution, ASR-related interaction events, usability, acceptance, and 1-month reproducibility of workflow execution. Results All participants completed both acquisitions without adverse events or safety-relevant events requiring interruption of the experimental workflow. End-effector recognition accuracy remained high, attention-recall events were infrequent, screen-based visual tasks were successfully administered and logged, and usability and acceptance outcomes were favorable, with low anxiety toward the robotic platform. Discussion These findings support the feasibility of using a therapist-supervised robotic platform as an integrated tool for structured interaction, head-orientation monitoring, rehabilitation-oriented task delivery, and quantitative logging. The study presents a preclinical evaluation of system architecture, safety-aware interaction design, and workflow robustness. Future work is organized in two stages: a dedicated acceptance and robustness protocol in healthy controls to formally test interaction acceptance, speech-recognition robustness, and safety-relevant failure handling, followed by a true rehabilitation protocol in post-stroke patients with hemispatial inattention, including therapist-supervised exercise adaptation.

nodes.name: OCE: an optimization convergence metric for LiDAR SLAM degeneracy detection
nodes.venue: Autonomous Intelligent Systems
nodes.abstract: Abstract LiDAR-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems suffer from environment-induced degeneracy in geometrically self-similar scenes such as tunnels and cylindrical structures, where the point cloud registration problem becomes ill-conditioned. Existing degeneracy detection methods predominantly rely on eigenvalue analysis of the Hessian matrix, which assesses geometric conditioning at a fixed linearization point. However, in semi-degenerate environments containing partial but sufficient geometric constraints, these methods tend to produce false positive detections because measurement noise inflates eigenvalues and obscures the contribution of minor structural features. In this paper, we propose the Optimization Convergence Efficiency (OCE) metric, which evaluates the relative contraction of the directional optimizer gradient across Levenberg-Marquardt evaluations and directly characterizes the convergence response of LiDAR registration along the monitored state direction. The proposed method is evaluated through controlled simulation with ground-truth-based quantitative assessment and real-world UAV experiments in a wind-turbine tower and a long tunnel. In the nominal simulation, OCE achieves 98.21% recall with a 2.33% false-positive rate, compared with 100% recall and a 49.42% false-positive rate for the conventional eigenvalue-ratio detector. Controlled measurement-noise experiments further demonstrate that OCE maintains substantially lower false-alarm rates as spectral discrimination becomes less reliable. These results show that OCE can retain usable LiDAR pose estimates in semi-degenerate environments while reliably identifying actual registration failure.

nodes.name: LTGC-Diff: A Local-Token and Global-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Model for SAR-Assisted Remote Sensing Image Cloud Removal
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Cloud contamination in optical remote sensing imagery can obscure land-surface information and induce structural blurring and spectral shifts, thereby seriously affecting subsequent land-cover interpretation and quantitative analysis. To address the instability of optical image restoration under complex cloud occlusion and the difficulty of effectively exploiting SAR auxiliary information, this paper proposes LTGC-Diff, a latent diffusion model for SAR-assisted remote sensing image cloud removal. The proposed method formulates cloud-free RGB image restoration as a latent denoising process constrained by multi-source observations. To better incorporate SAR auxiliary information into diffusion reconstruction, a diffusion-oriented conditional representation learning module is designed to transform SAR-derived features into effective conditional representations. In addition, a token-level structural condition adaptation module is designed to transform SAR patch representations into local structural guidance suitable for diffusion-based reconstruction. By jointly exploiting global scene-level guidance and local structure-aware constraints, the proposed model enables more stable and reliable recovery of cloud-obscured regions. Experimental results demonstrate that LTGC-Diff improves the structural consistency and restoration reliability of SAR-assisted optical remote sensing image cloud removal under complex cloud-contaminated scenarios. Specifically, LTGC-Diff achieves a PSNR of 32.87 dB while maintaining improved structural and spectral consistency, demonstrating its effectiveness for SAR-assisted cloud removal.

nodes.name: Investigation on an Improved SegFormer with Multi-Module Fusion for Landslide Recognition in Remote Sensing Images
nodes.venue: Water
nodes.abstract: Landslides pose severe threats to life and property, necessitating rapid and accurate identification for effective hazard assessment and emergency response. This study proposes an improved SegFormer model for precise landslide extraction from high-resolution remote sensing imagery. To address the limitations of existing segmentation methods in handling complex backgrounds and irregular boundaries, the proposed framework integrates several structural enhancements. These include a squeeze-and-excitation module to suppress background noise, an auxiliary edge-fusion branch to capture explicit boundary details, and an adaptive feature gating mechanism to refine feature representation. The model is trained using focal loss to mitigate class imbalance and employs a three-stage recognition process, culminating in post-processing with dense conditional random fields for boundary refinement. Herein, the experimental results on a dataset of 100 high-resolution satellite images demonstrate that this approach outperforms the classical U-Net architecture and traditional thresholding techniques. The model achieved an accuracy of 0.976, a precision of 0.918, a recall of 0.947, and an F1-score of 0.932. These findings confirm that the proposed method offers exceptional accuracy and robustness, providing an effective automated tool for large-scale landslide detection in complex terrain.

nodes.name: Integrated multi-criteria decision analysis and bivariate statistical modeling for landslide susceptibility zonation in the northwestern Ethiopian highlands
nodes.venue: Discover Hazards
nodes.abstract: Landslides represent a critical geo-environmental hazard in the Ethiopian highlands, specifically within the Telemt, Janamora, and Beyeda districts, where they frequently result in fatalities and the destruction of vital infrastructure and agricultural land. This study integrated Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing data to perform landslide susceptibility mapping (LSM) using two distinct modeling approaches: the Frequency Ratio (FR) and the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). A total of 140 data points (98 for training (70%) and 42 for testing (30%)) were considered for modeling and validation. Eleven geo-environmental conditioning factors: Slope, rainfall, lithology, density of lineaments, curvature, aspect, normalized difference vegetation index, land use/land cover, distance to drainage, drainage density, and soil were analyzed to evaluate their influence on landslide occurrence. According to the AHP model, 13.69% and 26.91% of the study area were classified as very high and high susceptibility zones, respectively. In comparison, the FR model identified 12.09% as very high and 23.78% as high susceptibility zones. Both models underscored that steep slopes, porphyritic basalt unit, high lineament density, proximity to drainage systems, and concave terrain curvature are the primary drivers of slope instability. Conversely, gentle slopes, sandstone unit, and dense vegetation cover were strongly associated with low-susceptibility regions. Model performance was validated using the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve, yielding an Area Under the Curve (AUC) value of 0.812 for the AHP model and 0.793 for the FR model, alongside a prediction rate AUC value of 77.4% (0.774) for the AHP model and 70.4% for the FR model, confirming the predictive reliability of both methods. These results provide essential geospatial intelligence for policy-makers and stakeholders to guide disaster risk management, sustainable land-use planning, and targeted rehabilitation efforts in the region.

nodes.name: Groundwater Potential Mapping in Northwestern Nigeria: A Comparison of the Analytic Hierarchy Process and Galileo-Enhanced CAT-XGB
nodes.abstract: Global water scarcity intensifies the need for high-resolution groundwater assessment tools, yet traditional approaches struggle to reconcile qualitative expert weights with the extensive spatial coverage offered by remote sensing data. This study presents a comparative framework evaluating expert-driven Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (a ten-layer Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP)) against data-driven ensemble machine learning for groundwater potential mapping in the geologically complex terrain of Northwestern Nigeria. Standard thematic layers were integrated with embeddings from a pretrained remote sensing foundation model to train ensemble classifiers, with groundwater potential validated against Vertical Electrical Sounding (VES) data. The foundation-model-enhanced CAT-XGB ensemble achieved notable predictive performance, consistently outperforming standalone tree-based classifiers and traditional AHP. Spatial difference mapping revealed that the enhanced ensemble captured critical, localized hydrogeological anomalies smoothed over by expert-driven weighting. Bridging heuristic decision-making with foundation-model-enhanced machine learning significantly improves spatial precision and reliability, potentially providing a field-validated tool for optimizing borehole siting and sustainable aquifer management in data-scarce, geologically complex regions.

nodes.name: Function-Decoupled Environment-Gated Multimodal Fusion for Chlorophyll-a Retrieval in a Cold–Arid Shallow Lake
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Lake Ulansuhai is a eutrophic shallow lake in the cold–arid region of northern China, where shallow water depth, frequent wind disturbance, and heterogeneous optical conditions complicate satellite-based chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) retrieval. To improve retrieval under such complex observation conditions, this study develops a function-decoupled environment-gated fusion framework (FDEGF) that integrates optical, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), and meteorological observations through predefined computational roles. Sentinel-2 optical features form the direct retrieval pathway, Sentinel-1 SAR features provide auxiliary information, and ERA5 meteorological variables condition the participation of the auxiliary pathway at the sampling-event level. A satellite–ground matched dataset containing 287 valid observations from 2017 to 2019 was constructed for Lake Ulansuhai. Across 31 paired random train–test splits, FDEGF showed a generally positive absolute-error advantage relative to simplified fusion structures, reducing median MAE by 0.360–0.467μgL−1. Further analyses showed that model performance depended on the correspondence between event-level meteorological gating and the SAR auxiliary pathway, while the three input pathways exhibited differentiated model dependence. Under unseen-station validation, FDEGF retained positive spatial transferability within the lake. However, leave-one-sampling-event-out validation yielded a pooled R2 of −0.144 and no consistent advantage over the structural controls. These results indicate that explicitly separating direct retrieval, auxiliary information, and meteorological gating provides a structurally explicit strategy for multimodal Chl-a retrieval within the represented sampling-event domain, while transfer to previously unseen sampling events remains limited.

nodes.name: From granularity to consensus: Mitigating sample defects for Remote Sensing Image–Text Retrieval
nodes.venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Remote Sensing Image–Text Retrieval (RSITR) aims to retrieve remote sensing images or text descriptions when only one modality is available. Despite recent progress, existing RSITR methods often suffer from sample defects, which cause them to mistakenly treat semantically related pairs as negatives, thereby limiting the benefits of advanced feature representations. To tackle the sample defect issue, we propose a novel Dual-Granularity Consensus-guided False Negative Suppression Network (CFSN 2 ), which jointly improves cross-modal alignment and false negative (FN) learning. First, CFSN 2 extracts momentum-updated feature queues for both global and local representations, enabling temporally coherent and stable similarity estimation. Second, it models dual-granularity similarity distributions via Gaussian Mixture Models and detects potential FNs through probabilistic cross-granularity consensus. Finally, the detected FNs are dynamically reweighted based on their FN confidence, softly suppressing their gradients while preserving informative negatives for a balanced optimization process. Extensive experiments across three datasets show that CFSN 2 achieves strong overall retrieval performance, with R@1 scores of 19.12, 28.96, and 22.86 in image-to-text retrieval, and 15.02, 25.22, and 18.00 in text-to-image retrieval, respectively, compared with 26 baselines.

Explainable fine-grained feature enhancement framework for strawberry diagnostic decision making
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Plant Science
nodes.abstract: As the number of smart agricultural automation systems increases, accurate disease diagnosis is essential to maximize production efficiency. However, early-stage symptoms of strawberry diseases (e.g., Tipburn, Phytophthora blight, and Fusarium wilt) often manifest as low-contrast micro-symptoms that are visually similar to the inherent complex texture of strawberry leaves, leading to high technical difficulties in achieving an accurate diagnosis. Furthermore, providing an explanation for the diagnosis remains challenging, which hinders trust in field applications. We present EN-FDEA, a deep learning framework that integrates an EfficientNetV2 backbone with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and a Fine-grained Discriminative Enhancement (FDEA) module combining depthwise separable convolution, parallel feature amplification, and channel recalibration, and we evaluate it together with a provenance audit of the corpus on which it is trained. Parsing the acquisition metadata embedded in every file name showed that the 1,000 abnormal images of each disease originate from only 33–73 individual plants, and that normal and abnormal images share no greenhouse; under the image-level cross-validation used in the original design, 91.9–99.8% of abnormal plants appear in both the training and the test partition of a fold. All results reported here are therefore obtained under plant-disjoint cross-validation with five random seeds, with a site-disjoint arm as the strictest comparison. Removing plant leakage lowers balanced accuracy by up to 0.082 and removing site overlap by up to 0.173. Under the leakage-free protocol, EN-FDEA performs comparably to, and not reliably better than, its EfficientNetV2 backbone (mean paired balanced-accuracy differences of –0.013 to +0.012 across datasets and conditions); the only Holm-corrected significant advantage is Phytophthora blight under overexposure (+0.012, p = 0.047). Forensic analysis further shows that the elevated performance previously observed under synthetic overexposure is a property of the transform: a logistic-regression classifier using only global exposure statistics reaches balanced accuracies of 0.81–0.92, and models trained on original images transfer poorly to synthetic overexposure while transferring well to genuinely over-illuminated frames selected from the corpus itself. We report explanation faithfulness, calibration, and measured deployment cost, and we state where the corpus structure, rather than the model, bounds what can be concluded. Code, split definitions, and per-image predictions are released so that every number can be regenerated.

nodes.name: Electromagnetic Field Exposure
nodes.venue: Emerald Group Publishing Limited eBooks
nodes.abstract: The rapid evolution of mobile communication technologies, from legacy Second Generation (2G)/Third Generation (3G) systems to Fourth Generation (4G) and the ongoing deployment of Fifth Generation (5G), has fundamentally transformed both network architecture and human exposure to Electromagnetic Field (EMF).Each generational shift has introduced new radio access technologies, higher data rates, and more complex antenna systems, necessitating a reevaluation of exposure assessment methodologies.The advent of 5G, in particular, marks a significant paradigm shift due to the widespread use of Active Antenna System (AAS) with beamforming capabilities, Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (mMIMO) arrays, and dynamic spatial-temporal power allocation [1,2].In this chapter, exposure due to 5G and legacy telecommunication Base Stations (BSs) and devices is discussed.Section 6.1 presents how EMF exposure varies across space and time, showing increases due to network densification and high-traffic events.Data-driven methods, from Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to infinite-width neural networks, reconstruct exposure maps from sparse measurements, enabling accurate monitoring and forecasting.Section 6.2 examines 5G mMIMO exposure, detailing methodologies for measuring maximum and instantaneous levels, the influence of User Equipment (UE), Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) conditions, and Frequency Range 2 (FR2) frequencies, and explores predictions for future exposure under higher traffic scenarios.Section 6.4 discusses public risk perception of Radio Frequency (RF)-EMF exposure and Smart Radio Communications: Intelligence-Enabling Radio Communications for Seamless Inclusive Interactions,

nodes.name: Ecological Indicators Reveal Contrasting Post-Earthquake Recovery Trajectories and Resilience Across Mountain Ecosystems
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Net primary productivity (NPP) is a useful ecological indicator for evaluating ecosystem functioning and recovery after natural disturbance. Here, we used multi-source remote-sensing and environmental data from 2010 to 2024 to compare post-earthquake NPP recovery in the 2017 Jiuzhaigou and Milin earthquake regions. We integrated trend analysis, temporal persistence assessment, co-seismic landslide overlay, eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and locally weighted scatterplot smoothing (LOWESS)-based contribution-transition detection to compare NPP dynamics and environmental associations in the two earthquake-affected regions. The two regions exhibited contrasting responses. The slope of regional mean annual NPP decreased from 9.69 to 8.21 g C m−2 yr−2 between the pre- and post-earthquake periods in Jiuzhaigou, whereas it increased from 3.69 to 9.37 g C m−2 yr−2 in Milin. Hurst-based trend-persistence analysis indicated a higher proportion of sustained improvement and a lower proportion of degradation-related classes in Jiuzhaigou, whereas Milin showed more degradation-related classes. Within co-seismic landslide zones, sustained degradation dominated in both regions and was more extensive in Milin. XGBoost–SHAP results showed that pre-earthquake NPP was the most influential predictor in both regions, but the contributions of secondary predictors differed. Elevation made a larger relative contribution to the Jiuzhaigou model, whereas pre-earthquake NDVI, precipitation, and temperature made larger relative contributions to the Milin model. LOWESS analysis further revealed distinct nonlinear response transitions in temperature, precipitation, and elevation. These results demonstrate the value of combining NPP trends, temporal persistence, and model interpretation to compare vegetation productivity dynamics and inform assessments of post-earthquake functional recovery in mountain ecosystems.

nodes.name: Dataset of DInSAR wrapped phase signals for AI-based automated detection and classification of mass movements
nodes.venue: Scientific Data
nodes.abstract: Abstract With the growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in remote sensing of mass movements, open and suitable datasets for model training and validation are increasingly needed. Although Differential Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (DInSAR) is a widely used technique for studying mass movements, wrapped interferograms remain less exploited, and the importance of geomorphological expertise in their interpretation is not usually emphasised. In this work, we introduce a dataset of DInSAR wrapped phase signals designed to support the development of Deep Learning (DL) models for the automated detection and classification of active slow-moving mass movements. The dataset covers two selected wide areas in the Central European Alps and the Northern Apennines. It contains 4910 expert-annotated DInSAR wrapped phase signals derived from 92 Sentinel-1 interferograms with temporal baselines ranging from 6 days to 1 year, classified into nine distinct landslide and periglacial landform classes after careful geomorphological interpretation. This dataset is expected to support the scientific community in AI-based applications for mass movement research, while also serving as a benchmark for the generation of comparable datasets.
